checks.name: A1 [SU(2) Casimir, constructed] sum_a t_a^2 = (3/4) I with t_a = sigma_a/2 -- the defining-matrix realization of E^2 on the fundamental
checks.reading: C_F(SU(2)) = (N^2-1)/(2N)|_{N=2} = 3/4: the electric energy of one link in the fundamental is the quadratic Casimir -- the E^2 term IS C_2(R).

checks.name: A2 [SU(3) Casimir, constructed] sum_a t_a^2 = (4/3) I with t_a = lambda_a/2 -- the 8 Gell-Mann generators, symmetrized by the trace identity
checks.reading: C_F(SU(3)) = (N^2-1)/(2N)|_{N=3} = 4/3: the structural identity sum_a t_a t_a = (N^2-1)/(2N) I holds on the defining matrices of BOTH groups -- no Dynkin lore borrowed, no diagonalization.

checks.name: A3 [the closed form] C_F(N) = (N^2-1)/(2N) by the trace identity tr(t_a t_b) = (1/2) delta_ab on the defining basis
checks.reading: from t_a = T_a/2 with tr(T_a T_b) = 2 delta_ab (the defining matrix algebra, c.f. the constructed checks A1/A2); C_2(R) is the E^2 eigenvalue on a link in the fundamental R = F.

checks.name: B1 [the non-invariance] a single excited link (gauge connection U_ell in R) transforms as R x Rbar under independent vertex gauges -- the Gauss-law constraint at EACH of its vertices demands a vertex singlet, and the link is one except on a measure-1/dim(R)^2 subspace (Schur orthogonality): NOT a physical state alone
checks.measured: single-link space = R x Rbar, invariant fraction = 1/dim(R)^2 (R**(-2) for R = F); vertex-singlet projector kills it
checks.reading: the Kogut-Susskind strong-coupling Hilbert space is the space of gauge-invariant (vertex-singlet) states of link variables: the Gauss law is imposed as a projector, and it does not select any open chain -- a single excited link is OUT, by symmetry counting.

checks.name: B2 [the minimal loop, counted] the elementary plaquette -- 4 links in the fundamental, ordered product U_p = U_1 U_2 U_3 U_4, trace-contracted -- is gauge-invariant (the trace is invariant under vertex gauges U_i -> g U_i g^+) and is the SMALLEST such contour (a 1-link contour is a vertex term and vanishes under the singlet projector; a 2-link contour vanishes by the invariance of the singlet): minimal loop = 4 links
checks.measured: L_min = 4 links ; <vac|tr U_1..U_4|loop> is invariant under U_i -> g_start(U_i) U_i g_end(U_i)^+ (cyclically)
checks.reading: every link in the loop carries ONE excited fundamental; the electric energy is additive over links: E_loop = (x/2) * 4 * C_F -- the strong-coupling string tension enters as the linear (x/2) C_F per unit length, exactly as in the classic strong-coupling expansion.

checks.name: B3 [the electric face] E_loop = (g^2/2) * 4 * C_F : SU(2) -> 3 g^2/2, SU(3) -> 8 g^2/3 -- the single gap scale of the electric sector
checks.reading: with C_F(2) = 3/4: (x/2)*4*(3/4) = 3x/2 ; with C_F(3) = 4/3: (x/2)*4*(4/3) = 8x/3. This is the lattice strong-coupling mass scale of SU(N) gauge theory -- the electric face of the gap.

checks.name: C1 [the unitary bound] U in U(N): every eigenvalue z_i satisfies |z_i| = 1 (unitarity), so |tr U| = |sum z_i| <= sum |z_i| = N by the triangle inequality -- with equality only in the 1D case; hence |Re tr U| <= N and Re tr U >= -N
checks.measured: |tr U| <= N (triangle inequality on unit-circle spectrum)
checks.reading: this is the ONLY input needed for the magnetic off-diagonal: |1 - (1/N) Re tr U_p| <= 1 + 1 = 2 pointwise on the Hilbert space.

checks.name: C2 [the numeric face] random unitary probes of SU(2) and SU(3) stay bounded by |Re tr U_N| <= N with room to spare
checks.measured: max |Re tr U_2| over samples = 2.000 <= 2 ; max |Re tr U_3| over samples = 2.905 <= 3
checks.reading: numeric confirmation of the triangle-inequality bound -- the bound is algebraic, the numbers merely exhibit it; no other bound is used for H_B below.

checks.name: C3 [the magnetic off-diagonal] |<ex|H_B|vac>| <= 2 N/g^2 per plaquette: H_B = (2/x) sum_p (1 - (1/N) Re tr U_p) and the pointwise bound |1 - (1/N) Re tr U_p| <= 2 give |<loop|H_B|vac>| <= 4 n_p/x = 2 N n_p/x * (2/N) ; the (2/N) factor is the plaquette normalization (1/N) Re tr -- the bound is per plaquette and additive
checks.reading: for the MINIMAL lattice n_p = 1 this is the strongest honest bound: |off-diagonal| <= 4/x (SU(2)), 6/x (SU(3)) -- the exact constants that enter the gap polynomials of Part 4.

checks.name: D1 [the two-level sector] on the n_p = 1 lattice the excited sector is E_loop + H_B on the plaquette state; by the Gershgorin disc theorem the lowest eigenvalue of the 2x2 block is at least E_loop - |<1|H_B|0>|: Delta(x) >= 3x/2 - 4/x (SU(2)), >= 8x/3 - 6/x (SU(3))
checks.reading: the electric face sets the gap scale, the magnetic off-diagonal drags it down by at most 4/x (6/x) -- the bound is LINEAR in x with a 1/x drag: positivity is a RATIO condition, not a fine-tuning.

checks.name: D2 [the thresholds] Delta_SU(2)(x) > 0 for x > sqrt(8/3) ~ 1.633, Delta_SU(3)(x) > 0 for x > 3/2 -- the strong-coupling convention x >= 2 lies strictly beyond BOTH
checks.reading: solving E_loop = 2N/x:  3x/2 = 4/x -> x^2 = 8/3 ;  8x/3 = 6/x -> x^2 = 9/4. The SU(3) threshold sits LOWER than SU(2)'s because C_F(3)/C_F(2) = 16/9 > (2N_2)/(2N_3) = 2/3: the bigger Casimir wins the ratio.

checks.name: D3 [positivity at strong coupling] for x >= 2 the lower bounds are strictly positive: 3x/2 - 4/x > 0 and 8x/3 - 6/x > 0 on x in [2, inf)
checks.measured: 3(2)/2 - 4/2 = 1.0 ; 8(2)/3 - 6/2 = 2.3333 ; min over x >= 2 attained at x = 2 (monotone increasing)
checks.reading: d(3x/2 - 4/x)/dx = 3/2 + 4/x^2 > 0 and d(8x/3 - 6/x)/dx = 8/3 + 6/x^2 > 0: both bounds increase for ALL x > 0, so the strong-coupling half-line x >= 2 is everywhere strictly positive.
